judged_text: The existing-attendee dedup compares guest === attendee.email case-sensitively while attendee emails are stored exactly as entered, so the write path and the compare path disagree on canonical form. Re-adding an existing attendee with different casing (John@X.com vs john@x.com) passes the filter, creating a duplicate Attendee row for the same person, who then receives both a full AttendeeScheduledEmail (as a 'new' guest) and an AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (as an existing one) for the same event.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees via `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`, which is case-sensitive and does not canonicalize emails. Since attendee emails are stored as-entered (`createMany` uses `email: guest`), adding the same address with different casing can bypass the filter and create a duplicate attendee row. This also impacts `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`: it checks `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` case-sensitively, so the original-cased attendee and the newly inserted differently cased attendee can receive different email templates (AttendeeAddGuestsEmail vs AttendeeScheduledEmail), resulting in two emails to what is effectively the same mailbox.
